<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs` from the code: do not edit. -->

Every diagnostic carries a code: the one to name in `[rules]` of `pgzest.toml` to change its severity, or in a `-- pgzest-disable-next-line <code>` comment to silence it at one place.

## Analysis

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `parse-error` | SQL that does not parse: the statement is skipped, with the parser's message. |
| `column-not-found` | Column reference that resolves to no column in scope (PostgreSQL `42703`). |
| `ambiguous-column` | Column reference that several relations in scope provide (`42702`): qualify it. |
| `table-not-found` | Relation that does not exist at this point (`42P01`). |
| `function-not-found` | Function or operator with no overload matching the argument types (`42883`). |
| `ambiguous-function` | Call that several overloads match equally (`42725`): cast an argument. |
| `type-mismatch` | Types PostgreSQL would refuse: a value assigned to a column of another type, `CASE`/`UNION`/`ARRAY` branches without a common type, an impossible cast, a non-boolean condition, a procedure called as a function… (a comparison without a matching operator is a `function-not-found`, as PostgreSQL reports it). |
| `parameter-not-found` | `$n` beyond the parameters of the routine (`42P02`). |
| `default-not-allowed` | `DEFAULT` outside an `INSERT … VALUES` or an `UPDATE … SET`. |
| `generated-column` | Value written to a generated column, or a generated column used in a generation expression. |
| `subquery-columns` | Subquery returning more columns than its context takes (`42601`). |
| `values-columns` | `VALUES` rows of different lengths. |
| `set-operation-columns` | Branches of a `UNION`, `INTERSECT` or `EXCEPT` with different numbers of columns. |
| `not-analyzed` | What the analysis does not cover, stated (information): no conclusion is drawn from it, and nothing is guessed. |

## PL/pgSQL

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `empty-function-body` | Routine whose body is empty (PL/pgSQL refuses it). |
| `trigger-no-context` | Trigger function no `CREATE TRIGGER` of the analyzed files attaches: `NEW` and `OLD` have no table to take their type from. |
| `undeclared-variable` | Variable used without being declared. |
| `raise-arguments` | `RAISE` whose `%` placeholders and arguments do not match in number. |

## Parsing

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `unparsable-statement` | Statement the parser could not read: either valid PostgreSQL outside the supported scope, or a syntax error. Level controlled by `[parse] unparsable`. |
| `unsupported-statement` | Valid statement deliberately not modeled in the AST (GRANT, …). Level controlled by `[parse] unsupported`. |
| `unparsed-function-body` | PL/pgSQL body the parser could not read: the routine is replayed, its body is not analyzed. Level controlled by `[parse] unparsable`. |

## Named queries

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `query-header-invalid` | Malformed `-- name:` header (name, cardinality, position). |
| `query-without-name` | SQL placed outside a named query in a query file. |
| `query-empty` | Header without SQL. |
| `query-multiple-statements` | More than one statement under the same header. |
| `query-duplicate-name` | Two queries with the same name in a file. |
| `query-mixed-parameters` | `$name` and `$1` in the same query. |
| `query-parameter-gap` | Positional parameters with a gap (`$1`, `$3` without `$2`). |
| `query-file-extension` | File in `[queries] directory` that is not a `.sql`. |
| `query-parameter-invalid` | Malformed parameter (`$0`, `$pageId`). |
| `query-not-describable` | Query the describer does not cover (other than SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CALL). |
| `query-parameter-untyped` | Parameter whose type no usage determines. |
| `query-cardinality-mismatch` | Declared cardinality incompatible with the query's. |

## Catalog (DDL replay)

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `type-not-found` | Referenced type not found in the catalog (neither built-in, nor from an active extension, nor declared by the project). |
| `object-not-found` | Altered or dropped object that does not exist at this point of the replay. |
| `object-already-exists` | Object created while it already exists (without `IF NOT EXISTS` / `OR REPLACE`). |
| `schema-not-found` | Nonexistent schema. |
| `extension-unavailable` | Extension whose catalog pgzest does not ship for this version. |
| `ambiguous-routine` | Routine name without a signature that designates several overloads. |
| `dependent-objects` | Drop refused by PostgreSQL for lack of `CASCADE` (dependent objects). |
| `ddl-not-replayed` | DDL in a `DO` block that the replay could not apply: condition not evaluable on the catalog, dynamic SQL, loop, unanalyzed body. The catalog may then differ from the database's. |
| `migration-header-invalid` | Migration header `-- pgzest: postgres=… extensions=…` malformed, duplicated or misplaced. |
| `migration-header-mismatch` | Migration header inconsistent with the replayed state: an extension announced but absent or active but not announced, routines generated at another `log=` level. |
| `migration-without-header` | Migrations without a `-- pgzest:` header: analyzed with the configured version (reported once). |
| `schema-drift` | Declarative schema the migrations do not reach: a migration remains to be generated (`pgzest migrate create`), or a change cannot be expressed automatically. |
| `query-row-mismatch` | Query declared to return the rows of another one (`-> other`) whose columns do not match (name, type, nullability). |
| `view-not-typed` | View columns whose types the query analysis did not establish. |

## Macros

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `macro-error` | Macro invocation that cannot be expanded: unknown macro or fragment, header not matching the macro's pattern, missing `}`, a directive pgzest cannot rewrite. |
| `not-isolated` | Dynamic SQL (`EXECUTE`) in a body with isolated temp tables: what it runs is not rewritten, and may see the rows of other runs. |
| `not-logged` | What a logged build cannot log: a routine whose body pgzest cannot instrument (it runs unlogged), or the routines a `RETURN` of a polymorphic result calls (logged as called by the caller). |

## Migration risks

Reported on the statements of a generated migration (`pgzest migrate create`), and listed in its `!! TO ADAPT` header when the migration may lose data or fail on a populated database.

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `M001` | `NOT NULL` column added without a default: fails if the table has rows. |
| `M002` | Dropped column, with its data. |
| `M003` | Dropped table, with its data. |
| `M004` | Column type changed: table rewritten, conversion possibly impossible. |
| `M005` | `SET NOT NULL`: full scan, fails on a null value. |
| `M006` | Index built without `CONCURRENTLY` on an existing table: writes blocked during the build. |
| `M007` | Constraint added to an existing table, checked on every row under lock (`NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE` avoids it). |

## Lint

Style and practice rules (`pgzest lint`).

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `L001` | SELECT * used outside a CTE definition. SELECT * makes schema changes silently break downstream consumers. Prefer explicitly listing columns. |
| `L002` | CREATE TABLE without a primary key constraint. Every table should have a primary key so rows can be uniquely identified and to support replication, foreign keys, and ORM ergonomics. |
| `L003` | Table or column name is not snake_case. PostgreSQL folds unquoted identifiers to lower-case. Quoted mixed-case names are error-prone and break convention. Enforce snake_case throughout. |
| `L004` | NOT IN (subquery) is used. `NOT IN (SELECT ...)` returns no rows if the subquery contains any NULL, which is almost never the intended behaviour. Use `NOT EXISTS (...)` instead. |
| `L005` | Foreign key column without a covering index. Unindexed FK columns cause full table scans on every FK lookup and CASCADE operation. Always index the referencing column(s). |
| `L006` | LIKE/ILIKE pattern with a leading wildcard. LIKE '%foo' cannot use a standard B-tree index and causes a full table scan. Use a full-text index (GIN + tsvector) or a trigram index (pg_trgm) instead. |
| `L007` | Aggregate function mixed with bare column references without GROUP BY. `SELECT count(*), user_id FROM tasks` lacks `GROUP BY user_id`: PostgreSQL refuses it. |
| `L008` | ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN NOT NULL without a DEFAULT value. On PostgreSQL < 11, this rewrites the entire table. Even on modern PG, it acquires an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock while the NOT NULL constraint is validated. Always provide a DEFAULT when adding NOT NULL columns to existing tables. |
| `L009` | JOIN table that is never referenced in SELECT, WHERE, or ORDER BY. An unused JOIN wastes I/O and can produce unexpected row multiplication. Remove the JOIN or verify that it was intended. |

## Plugin `rls-enforcer`

Enabled by `[plugins] builtin = { rls-enforcer = {} }`.

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `rls/table-without-rls` | Table created without row-level security enabled (warning: RLS may be enabled separately, by `ALTER TABLE … ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`). |
| `rls/select-star` | `SELECT *` in an application query: list the columns. |
